dialect.detail: Standard COBOL-85 style; no vendor-specific extensions detected. Uses FUNCTION RANDOM, EVALUATE, PERFORM VARYING with TEST AFTER — all COBOL-85 features. Likely compiled with GnuCOBOL or similar open-source compiler given the game context.
evidence: no EXEC CICS/SQL, no COMP-3, no vendor directives

purpose.domain_detail: Text-based Minesweeper game implemented in COBOL
purpose.summary: A fully playable text-based Minesweeper game. The program initialises a minefield of configurable size (beginner/intermediate/veteran), randomly places mines, accepts player commands to open/flag/suspect cells, checks for win/lose conditions, and displays the board to the terminal.

notable_features: FUNCTION RANDOM used for mine placement with time-based seed
Stack-based flood-fill algorithm (CHK-STACK) for opening empty cells
EVALUATE for command dispatch and level selection
DEBUG SECTION with commented-out mine display
No EXEC SQL, no EXEC CICS, no COMP-3
verdict.notes: The program is a self-contained Minesweeper game, clearly a student or hobbyist exercise. The filename and PROGRAM-ID 'mineswpr' confirm this. The flood-fill uses a manual stack (CHK-STACK) with up to 200 entries, which may overflow on large boards. The edge-detection logic only marks one edge per axis (not both), which could be a bug for non-edge cells. No ENVIRONMENT DIVISION is present. The comment 'COINBOLLER' in the welcome message appears to be a playful name for the game.
